note: The Dwell's people are tools/worlds/homelands.json's (Sylhilthis' Dwell): Elder Hoshuk gives the first two, Reedwarden Tsumo beside him the three hunts; Netmender Ishiko (west of the elder) is the outfitter, Coachman Dobu keeps the stable on the south sand. The hunts are across the causeway, on the shore south-east of the island: the marsh rats where the causeway lands, the mudfang basilisks on the flats south of them, the blue basilisk Gulpjaw alone on the east shore. Levels 7-20 (2026-11-11): Reedwarden Tsumo gives L7-L15, Elder Hoshuk the L20 path; their objectives are on the Homelands' shared ground, the Goldfeather Eyrie (Dobu's coach), at the head of the rivers: drift rat fur and a badger pelt, Dunmore's ore with Ishiko's reed cord and rime spider silk, four frostpaw cubs off the river ice, the Rimeheart's shard (it chilled the river), then Halvek and Quartermaster Dunmore's stores against the raiders.

L1.name: A Charm for the Shell
offer: Another young one, fresh from the egg and still soft in the shell! Every kappa of the Dwell wears a shell charm before it first leaves the island.
Netmender Ishiko strings them from river shell and reed cord. She mends her nets on the sand just west of here.
Will you fetch your charm and show it to me?
L1.declined: The Dwell will wait for you.
L1.started: Go on, then. Ishiko is on the sand just west of here.

piece.name: river-shell charm
piece.description: A chip of river shell on a reed cord. Every young kappa of the Dwell wears one.

fetch.journal: Ask Netmender Ishiko, west of Elder Hoshuk, for a river-shell charm.
fetch.says: The elder sent you? Bend your neck. There: river shell for a hard back, reed cord so the water does not take it. No charge for a young one.

show.journal: Show the river-shell charm to Elder Hoshuk.
show.says: It hangs well on you. Wear it, and the river will know you for one of ours.

L2.name: Bound to the Dwell
offer: The water carries young ones far, and it does not always carry them back. Have Spiritmaster Oruko bind your spirit to the Dwell, so that you wake here if you fall.
Then give your name to Coachman Dobu for his ledger. His coach runs to Freeport and to the other homes of the Homelands, for those their stables know.
Will you see them both and come back to me?
L2.declined: Then wade in the shallows until you do.
L2.started: Oruko stands on the west sand, past Ishiko. Dobu keeps his coach on the sand south of here.

bind.journal: Have Spiritmaster Oruko, on the sand west of the elder, bind your spirit to the Dwell.
bind.says: It is done. Should you fall, you will wake here on our sand. Now go and give Coachman Dobu your name.

ledger.journal: Give your name to Coachman Dobu, south of the elder, for his ledger.
ledger.says: Welcome to my stable, young one. My coach runs to Freeport and to every other home of the Homelands, for travelers whose names their ledgers hold. Yours is in mine now.

says: Good. Now the Dwell will always draw you home, as the sea draws the river.
Dobu's coach will carry you to Freeport if its ledger knows you, but the way down the river to Rivervale is earned. Reedwarden Tsumo, beside me, has work for you.

L3.name: Rats in the Reeds
offer: So you are the young one Hoshuk spoke of. Good. Marsh rats have dug into the reeds where our causeway meets the shore, and they gnaw the nets we dry there.
Cross the causeway to the south-east and bring me three of their tails. Then I will teach you something worth knowing.
Will you hunt them?
L3.declined: Then the nets will be gnawed to string.
L3.started: Three tails. Keep your shell between you and their teeth.

drop.name: marsh rat tail
drop.description: The tail of a marsh rat from the shore where the Dwell's causeway lands.

hunt.journal: Take three marsh rat tails from the marsh rats on the shore south-east of the Dwell, where the causeway lands.

give.journal: Bring three marsh rat tails to Reedwarden Tsumo.
give.says: Three tails, and not a crack in your shell. You can fight. Now watch closely, and learn this.

L4.name: A Young One's Arms
offer: Bare claws will not serve you down the river. I will make you proper gear, but you will fetch what I need.
Netmender Ishiko has reed cord and a good shaft for me. Then take a scale from the mudfang basilisks on the flats south of the shore, past the rats.
Will you bring me all three?
L4.declined: Then keep to your claws, and to the shallows.
L4.started: Cord and a shaft from Ishiko, a scale from the mudfangs. Go.

items.name: braided reed cord
items.description: A length of river reed, braided tight by the Dwell's netmenders.

materials.journal: Ask Netmender Ishiko for the braided reed cord and the wooden shaft.
materials.says: For Tsumo? Here, a braid of reed cord and a straight shaft. Tell him the nets come first next time.

drop.name: mudfang scale
drop.description: A broad scale from a mudfang basilisk of the flats south of the Dwell's shore.

hunt.journal: Take a mudfang scale from the mudfang basilisks on the flats south of the Dwell, past the marsh rats.

give.journal: Bring the braided reed cord, the wooden shaft and the mudfang scale to Reedwarden Tsumo.
give.says: All three. Give me a moment... there. It is yours: carry it well.

L5.name: Old Gulpjaw
offer: One task more before the river takes you. A great blue basilisk we call Gulpjaw has dragged two of our netmenders off the east shore.
He lies alone on the bank east of where the causeway lands, and he bites first. Bring me his tooth, and I will teach you the last thing I have for a young one.
Will you hunt Gulpjaw?
L5.declined: He will not grow gentler while you wait.
L5.started: Over the causeway, then east along the shore. Do not let him get his jaws on your shell.

drop.name: Gulpjaw's tooth
drop.description: A long tooth of the blue basilisk Gulpjaw.

hunt.journal: Take Gulpjaw's tooth from the blue basilisk Gulpjaw on the shore south-east of the Dwell, east of the causeway.

give.journal: Bring Gulpjaw's tooth to Reedwarden Tsumo.
says: Gulpjaw's own tooth! The netmenders will work the east shore again. You are a young one no longer.
Learn this, and see Gatekeeper Kabbo on the causeway when you are ready to go down the river.

flight.name: Down the River
offer: The current is fair for Tunaria. The halflings of Rivervale welcomed the first of us who went down the river, and they will train you as their own.
You have earned the passage, young one. I will set you down among your own guild in Rivervale, and your spirit will rest there.
Shall I send you down the river?
flight.declined: The river will wait for you.
flight.started: Swim strong, and keep your shell clean!
flight.journal: Tell Gatekeeper Kabbo when you are ready to go down the river to Rivervale.

L7.name: Two Tasks Upriver
offer: You have grown into your shell. Good. The rivers of the Homelands all run from the cold, and at the Goldfeather Eyrie the Homelands keep a hunters' outpost on the frozen river.
Ride Dobu's coach there. Bring me three clumps of drift rat fur and a badger's pelt, from the snow east of the outpost. The netmenders want them for the winter.
Will you go up to the ice?
L7.declined: The ice will not melt while you wait.
L7.started: Keep your shell dry. Cold water is slow to forgive.

drop.name: drift rat fur
drop.description: A clump of white fur from a drift rat of the Goldfeather Eyrie's snow.

hunt.journal: Take three clumps of drift rat fur from the drift rats east of the Eyrie outpost.

drop.name: snowfield badger pelt
drop.description: The thick pelt of a snowfield badger of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take a snowfield badger pelt from the badgers on the snow east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the drift rat fur and the badger pelt to Reedwarden Tsumo.
give.says: Fur and a pelt, and not a crack in your shell. The netmenders will be warm. Now watch closely, and learn this.

L10.name: Ore from the Eyrie
offer: River clay makes a fine pot and a poor blade. You need better arms now, and the Eyrie outpost has the ore for it.
Ask Quartermaster Dunmore there for ore, and Ishiko here for her reed cord. Then a skein of silk from the rime spiders north-east of the outpost, to bind it.
Will you bring me all three?
L10.declined: Then keep your old arms oiled.
L10.started: Ore, cord and silk. Mind the river ice.

materials.journal: Ask Quartermaster Dunmore at the Eyrie outpost for ore for Tsumo.
materials.says: Tsumo's word came by the coach. Here, good ore. Do not let it fall through the ice: I will not fish for it.

items.name: braided reed cord
items.description: A length of river reed, braided tight by the Dwell's netmenders.

materials.journal: Ask Netmender Ishiko for braided reed cord.
materials.says: More cord for Tsumo? Here. He will owe me a net by the end of this.

drop.name: rime spider silk
drop.description: A skein of frosted silk from a rime spider of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take a skein of silk from the rime spiders north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the iron ore, the braided reed cord and the rime spider silk to Reedwarden Tsumo.
give.says: All three. Give me a moment... there. It is yours. Better than river clay, I promise you.

L13.name: Cubs on the River Ice
offer: The frostpaw cubs north of the Eyrie outpost have taken to the river ice, where the outpost's hunters cut their fishing holes. They have mauled two already.
Drive them off the ice. Four should teach the rest.
Will you hunt the frostpaw cubs?
L13.started: Four. Do not fall through the ice.

hunt.journal: Kill four frostpaw cubs on the snow north of the Eyrie outpost.

back.says: Four, and the fishing holes are open again. A kappa looks after the water, wherever it runs. Learn this.

L15.name: The Cold at the River's Source
offer: The water at the Dwell has run colder all season. It comes from the ice caves north-east of the Eyrie outpost, where a thing the hunters call the Rimeheart walks.
Break it, and bring me a shard. I would see what has chilled our river.
Will you face the Rimeheart?
L15.started: Go with others. That cold cracks shells.

drop.name: shard of the Rimeheart
drop.description: A shard of blue ice that never melts, broken from the Rimeheart.

hunt.journal: Take a shard from the Rimeheart, in the ice caves north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the shard of the Rimeheart to Reedwarden Tsumo.
give.says: So this is what chilled the river. It will warm now. You are no young one, %p. Learn this.

L20.name: Up the River and Home
offer: Tsumo says your shell has hardened. A kappa of the Dwell goes once to the head of the river, and helps whoever keeps it, before it goes down to the sea.
Go to Warden Halvek at the Eyrie outpost, and do as he asks. Then come home to me, and choose your path.
Will you go up the river?
L20.declined: The river runs all year. Go when you are ready.

road.journal: Find Warden Halvek at the Eyrie outpost.
road.says: Hoshuk sends a kappa? Good. The Goldfeather raiders robbed Dunmore's stores again. Ask him what they took.

road.journal: Ask Quartermaster Dunmore at the Eyrie outpost what the raiders took.
road.says: Half my winter stores, gone up to their eyrie. I want their war-talons, two of them, so they know we can reach them.

drop.name: Goldfeather war-talon
drop.description: A war-talon of the Goldfeather aviaks, bound in gold thread.

hunt.journal: Take two war-talons from the Goldfeather raiders round the eyrie east of the Eyrie outpost.

handin.journal: Bring the two war-talons to Quartermaster Dunmore.
handin.says: Two talons! I'll hang them over my stores. Go home, kappa. Tell Hoshuk the outpost owes the Dwell.

final.journal: Return to Elder Hoshuk at the Dwell.
final.says: You went up the river and came down it again. That is the whole of a kappa's life, done young. The Dwell has one more gift.
